name: tcp_do_segment
prose: tcp_do_segment(tp, m, th, drop_hdrlen, tlen, iptos) is the main TCP input state machine for a segment on an existing connection; it returns void and always consumes m. The caller must hold the inpcb write lock inside a network epoch (NET_EPOCH_ASSERT, INP_WLOCK_ASSERT); tp->t_state must be after LISTEN and not TIME_WAIT (the two KASSERTs at tcp_input.c:1547-1550). It first drops (goto drop) a segment with both SYN and FIN when V_drop_synfin is set, and sends a reset (goto dropwithreset) for a segment with ACK in SYN_SENT whose acknowledgement is outside (iss, snd_max]. It then updates idle and receive time, scales the window, processes ECN and parses the TCP options, and goes through the state-dependent checks and processing (header prediction for the common established-connection cases, SYN_SENT and SYN_RECEIVED handling, PAWS/timestamp and sequence-window checks and trimming, RST handling, ACK processing, window update, data queueing via tcp_reass or direct append, FIN handling); this slice (lines 2113-2375 of the file) shows only the middle part of that logic. Along the way it may call tcp_drop or tcp_close, which can free tp, or tcp_twstart, after which it returns. The function leaves through one of these exits, all verified at tcp_input.c:3371-3438: (1) after tcp_twstart it returns; (2) check_delack: if TF_DELACK is set it is cleared and the delayed-ACK timer is armed, the inpcb write lock is released and it returns (m is consumed earlier on that path); (3) dropafterack: for SYN_RECEIVED with an out-of-range ACK it takes dropwithreset, otherwise it sets TF_ACKNOW, calls tcp_output, releases the inpcb lock and frees m; (4) dropwithreset: tcp_dropwithreset(m, th, tp, tlen) (which consumes m) and the inpcb lock is released if tp is non-NULL; (5) drop: the inpcb lock is released if tp is non-NULL and m is freed. After tcp_output at the end of normal processing (when needoutput or TF_ACKNOW) it falls into check_delack.

name: tcp_default_output
prose: tcp_default_output(tp) is the default stack's TCP output routine (the packet calls it tcp_output; tcp_output.c:186-1741). It decides whether and what to send for connection tp and sends at most the data allowed by the windows; it must be called with the inpcb write lock held inside a network epoch, and the mbuf for a segment is built inside the function. Return values: for a TCP-offload connection (TF_TOE) it returns tcp_offload_output(tp); for a TFO connection in SYN_SENT or SYN_RECEIVED that has already sent its SYN or SYN|ACK and is not retransmitting it returns 0; when it finds nothing to send (label just_return) it returns 0; if a UDP tunnelling port is set for the connection but the tunnelling port has been removed it returns EHOSTUNREACH (after unlocking the send buffer); otherwise it builds a segment and sends it with ip_output or ip6_output. If an error is produced when building or sending (EMSGSIZE when the IP header chain and the TCP header would not fit in one segment (RFC 7112 case), ENOBUFS for mbuf allocation failures, a failed TCP-MD5 digest calculation (the mbuf is freed), or the error from ip_output/ip6_output), control reaches the common 'out' code. There: if the segment had TH_RST it returns 0 whatever the error was (the sequence variables are not advanced). Otherwise, unless in persist-forced state, snd_nxt is advanced over the sent SYN, FIN and len bytes (a SACK retransmission instead pulls snd_nxt up to the scoreboard) and snd_max, the round-trip timing and the retransmit timer (or, for a zero-length send with queued data and no timers, the persist timer) are updated; in the persist-forced case only snd_max is advanced. After an ip_output error the advance is rolled back (including the SACK rxmit pointer and FIN) unless the send was a persist-forced one, the segment carried a SYN, or the error is EPERM. The error is then handled: EACCES and EPERM set t_softerror and return the error; ENOBUFS sets snd_cwnd to one segment and returns 0; EMSGSIZE clears TF_TSO if TSO was used and, when an MTU was learned from ip_output, updates the MSS and retries ('goto again'), else returns the error; EHOSTDOWN, EHOSTUNREACH, ENETDOWN and ENETUNREACH set t_softerror and return 0 if a SYN has been received (TCPS_HAVERCVDSYN) and return the error otherwise; every other error is returned. On success it counts the segment, updates rcv_adv and last_ack_sent, clears TF_ACKNOW and TF_DELACK, cancels the delayed-ACK timer and then loops ('goto again') if more data can be sent in the same call (sendalot), otherwise returns 0.

Return paths verified at 227, 240, 758, 892, 1530, 1685-1721, 1740. name: tcp_reass
prose: tcp_reass(tp, th, seq_start, tlenp, m) queues an out-of-order segment on tp's reassembly queue and, when possible, delivers in-sequence queued data to the socket receive buffer. The caller holds the inpcb write lock. If th is NULL it only tries to deliver already queued data (used after the connection becomes established). Otherwise seq_start and tlenp must be non-NULL, th->th_seq must be >= rcv_nxt (KASSERTs), *tlenp is the payload length and m the segment's mbuf chain, which the function always consumes (queued, appended to so_rcv, trimmed or freed). Drops that free m and return 0, setting *tlenp = 0 where noted: a zero-length segment without FIN, or a FIN-only segment before the connection is established (m freed, *tlenp unchanged); the mbuf-count limit reached when the segment is not the next expected one on an established connection (tcps_rcvreassfull, *tlenp = 0); a FIN that would end before the last queued segment (*tlenp = 0); data after a queued FIN (*tlenp = 0); the queue length limit reached (*tlenp = 0); a failed uma_zalloc for a new queue entry (*tlenp = 0). A segment completely overlapped by an existing queued one is dropped with return 0 and *seq_start and *tlenp set to that queued segment's start and length. Segments that join, replace or prepend to an existing queued entry update *seq_start and *tlenp to the resulting entry's start and length. A segment equal to rcv_nxt on an established connection that reaches new_entry is appended directly to so_rcv (or freed if SBS_CANTRCVMORE), rcv_nxt is advanced, TF_WAKESOR is set and the function returns the segment's FIN flag (0 or TH_FIN) without setting *seq_start or *tlenp. A segment that becomes a new separate queue entry is inserted with *seq_start and *tlenp left unchanged. After queueing, the 'present' step runs: if the connection is not established or the head entry does not start at rcv_nxt it returns 0; otherwise under the receive buffer lock it removes and delivers consecutive queue entries starting at rcv_nxt (freeing the data if SBS_CANTRCVMORE), advances rcv_nxt, updates t_segqlen and t_segqmbuflen, sets TF_WAKESOR and returns the TH_FIN bit of the last entry delivered.
note: reviewer round15 right: *seq_start is not set on the new-entry queueing path (tcp_reass.c:954-1045) nor on the direct in-order append path (955-967). Old prose also wrongly said the queue-limit drop paths set no *tlenp; tcp_reass.c:516-1115. slice cut the head

name: bbr_output_wtime
prose: bbr_output_wtime(tp, tv) is the BBR stack's output routine (bbr.c:11859-14067); the slice shows an interior fragment of it. Its documented return value is 0 on success and an errno on failure to send; a 0 return may mean nothing was sent (for example when the connection is waiting on the hpts pacer); a non-zero value is the error from ip_output/ip6_output; negative values (-EFAULT and -ENETDOWN at bbr.c:13175 and 13796) are returned to make the caller drop the connection. Other exits: tcp_offload_output for offloaded connections, early 'return 0' paths when the connection is on the pacer or timers handled it (the timer result is returned as retval if negative, else 0), EHOSTUNREACH when the UDP tunnelling port was removed, and the final return of the accumulated error (after ENOBUFS is converted to 0). The part shown works out how much to send (len) from the scoreboard (rsm, sack_rxmit), the flags and the windows; if len is not positive no segment is sent and, depending on state, persist mode may be entered.

name: bbr_set_sockopt
prose: bbr_set_sockopt(tp, sopt) handles setsockopt for the BBR stack. For IPPROTO_IP and IPPROTO_IPV6 levels and for any option name that is not one of the listed TCP_RACK_* / TCP_BBR_* / TCP_DELACK / TCP_DATA_AFTER_CLOSE options it returns tcp_default_ctloutput(tp, sopt). For the listed options it drops the inpcb write lock, copies an int in with sooptcopyin (returning that error with the lock NOT re-taken), re-takes the lock and returns ECONNRESET (lock released) if the inpcb was dropped or ENOPROTOOPT (lock released) if tp no longer uses the BBR stack. It then applies the value inside a switch on the option name: simple options store optval into the matching bbr field; others validate it (for example TCP_DELACK accepts 0, 1 or 2..99 and gives EINVAL for 100 or more, and may send an immediate ACK; TCP_BBR_POLICER_DETECT, TCP_BBR_TMR_PACE_OH and TCP_BBR_PACE_OH return EINVAL in the Google mode restrictions shown) and set error to EINVAL when the value or the current mode does not allow the change, leaving the field unchanged. Each option increments its option counter. The remaining part of the function (not in the slice) releases the lock and returns the error. The packet name bbr_setopt_switch does not exist: the slice is the inner switch of bbr_set_sockopt.

name: bbr_log_ack
prose: bbr_log_ack(tp, to, th, prev_acked) processes the scoreboard (rc_map of bbr_sendmap entries) for an incoming ACK and returns the number of bytes newly acknowledged by SACK blocks (sack_changed, possibly 0). If the segment has RST it returns 0 at once without writing *prev_acked. Otherwise, if th_ack advances beyond snd_una it updates the progress time; cumulatively acknowledged entries are removed from rc_map and rc_tmap (a fully acked entry is freed with bbr_free; a partly acked entry has r_start moved up to th_ack), with RTT samples taken (bbr_update_rtt) for entries not already SACKed and with rc_sacked, rc_lost_bytes, rc_lost, rc_lt_lost, rc_holes_rxt and the rc_next and rc_sacklast markers adjusted; for a SYN-ACK with no map and a timestamp echo it derives an initial RTT sample. After that it detects a peer that reneged (bbr_peer_reneges), and if the options carry SACK blocks it filters and sorts the valid blocks (recording D-SACK blocks with tcp_record_dsack), and processes each with bbr_proc_sack_blk, setting r_wanted_output when SACK data changed. At the end *prev_acked is set to p_acked, which is the sum of the sizes of scoreboard entries that had been SACKed earlier and are now cumulatively acked (not the total number of bytes cumulatively acked); if SACK changed the state and the connection is not in recovery it checks whether to enter recovery (bbr_check_recovery_mode), sets r_wanted_output and rc_resend; in recovery it may set rc_resend. The caller keeps ownership of its arguments.

name: rack_do_syn_recv
prose: rack_do_syn_recv(m, th, so, tp, to, drop_hdrlen, tlen, tiwin, thflags, nxt_pkt, iptos) processes a segment for a RACK-stack connection in SYN_RECEIVED. By its contract a return of 1 means the TCB has been dropped/unlocked (probably gone) and m consumed, and 0 means the TCB is still locked. Paths: a RST, or a FIN when t_fin_is_rst is set, returns ctf_process_rst(...) unchanged; an ACK with ack <= snd_una or > snd_max logs TCP_EI_STATUS_RST_IN_FRONT, calls ctf_do_dropwithreset and returns 1; for a TFO connection, a segment with both SYN and ACK is dropped with reset and returns 1, a SYN (not the initial one) while a RXT, TLP or RACK timer is running is dropped with ctf_do_drop and returns 0 (without such a timer, processing continues), and a segment with none of ACK, FIN, RST is dropped with ctf_do_drop and returns 0; a PAWS failure calls ctf_ts_check, and if it reports the segment handled the function returns its ret_val; a sequence number below irs logs RST_IN_FRONT, drops with reset and returns 1; ctf_drop_checks reporting a drop returns its ret_val; otherwise (when those helpers return 0) processing continues. Without the ACK bit it returns rack_process_data(...) (calling rack_cc_conn_init first for TFO). With ACK it counts a connect, completes the socket connection, applies window scaling, moves the state to ESTABLISHED (or FIN_WAIT_1 if TF_NEEDFIN), advances snd_una for the ACK of the SYN, flushes queued data with tcp_reass when the segment carries no data or FIN, takes an RTT sample from the timestamp echo, then returns ret_val if rack_process_ack reports a drop; if the state is FIN_WAIT_1 and our FIN was acknowledged it moves to FIN_WAIT_2 (with the 2MSL timer and soisdisconnected when no more data can be received); finally it returns rack_process_data(...).

name: rack_do_compressed_ack_processing
prose: rack_do_compressed_ack_processing(tp, so, m, nxt_pkt, tv) handles a compressed-ACK mbuf holding between 1 and TCP_COMP_ACK_ENTRIES ACK entries for a RACK-stack connection (rack.c:15494-16164; the slice shows its middle part). Each entry is treated as one of a cumulative-ack advance, an ACK behind the cumulative point, a window update or a duplicate ACK; cumulative and window state are advanced, RTT and SACK scoreboard updates are done, and recovery and congestion-control state are updated as entries are processed. The function always consumes m. Return values: 1 when the connection has been closed or dropped (tcp_close returned NULL, tcp_drop on a progress timeout, tcp_twstart in CLOSING, tcp_close in LAST_ACK, or tcp_output returned a negative value); and 0 otherwise, in which case the TCB is still locked, and when nxt_pkt is non-zero the function returns 0 right after freeing m without sending output. When no further packet is pending, it may call tcp_output (when output is wanted, fast output is on or TF_ACKNOW is set), frees excess send-map entries and audits the timers before returning 0. A socket in a late state with no data left and TF2_DROP_AF_DATA set is reset by closing the connection and sending output from the closed state (the 'send_out_a_rst' path).

name: rack_get_pacing_delay
prose: rack_get_pacing_delay(rack, tp, len, rsm, segsiz, line) returns the pacing delay in microseconds (int32_t) to apply after sending len bytes; the slice shows its end. Besides computing the delay it may change pacing state: with hardware pacing enabled it may start, change or release a hardware rate (tcp_set_pacing_rate / tcp_chg_pacing_rate / tcp_rel_pacing_rate), set rc_pace_max_segs and r_ctl.crte, and update counters and logs. If rack->rc_always_pace is 0 (or the bandwidth estimate cannot be used, or the wanted rate is 0) the 'old method' is used: len divided by a per-ms rate derived from the cwnd and the minimum RTT or srtt, reduced by rack_slot_reduction, converted to microseconds and optionally adjusted by pace_to_fill_cwnd. With rc_always_pace set and a rate (fixed rate, delivery rate or an estimate from cwnd), the delay is derived from len and the wanted rate. In the part shown: when rack_limit_time_with_srtt is set and neither a fixed rate nor hardware pacing is in use, the delay is capped at the smoothed RTT (or RACK_INITIAL_RTO milliseconds converted to microseconds when there is no srtt); and when the hardware rate entry has seen ENOBUFS (rs_num_enobufs > 0), a boost delay (time_between times rack_enobuf_hw_boost_mult, limited to the range [rack_enobuf_hw_min, rack_enobuf_hw_max]) is added to the delay before it is returned. With rr_config 1 and a retransmission (rsm non-NULL) it returns rc_min_to without computing anything else. This tree adds a guard: a zero wanted rate falls back to the old method (bw division by zero avoided).

name: rack_fast_rsm_output
prose: rack_fast_rsm_output(tp, rack, rsm, ts_val, cts, ms_cts, tv, len, doing_tlp) sends a retransmission of the send-map entry rsm through the 'fast' path, using the mbuf offsets saved in rsm, with len bytes (normally one MSS) (the packet called it rack_output; the slice is the middle of this function, rack.c:18336-18878). On success it returns 0 after sending: it logs the output, counts the send (and TLP bookkeeping when doing_tlp), reduces the PRR send count, clears TF_ACKNOW and TF_DELACK, starts RTT timing if idle, and arms the hpts timer: with an ENOBUFS result the slot is (1 + rc_enobuf) ms, at least 10 ms (so the function still returns 0), otherwise the slot comes from rack_get_pacing_delay. A failure while building the segment (label failed) frees the partial mbuf and returns -1. Other errors from the output call do not change the return value 0.

name: rack_output
prose: rack_output(tp) is the RACK stack's output routine (rack.c:19582-22517; the packet slices show interior fragments). It runs with the inpcb write lock held inside a network epoch. Return values: for an offloaded connection tcp_offload_output(tp); 0 for a TFO connection in SYN_RECEIVED that has only sent its SYN|ACK, when the connection is in persist, when an ACK is required after a timeout, when the connection is on the hpts and the pacer should not be overridden, and after rack_start_hpts_timer for the TFO SYN case; when the timer processing (rack_process_timers) wants the connection dropped it returns the negative value it returned and otherwise 0; the fast-output path may return its result directly. If a segment is built and the output call fails: EPERM and EACCES set t_softerror and return the error; ENOBUFS arms a pacing slot of (1 + rc_enobuf) ms (at least 10 ms) and goes on with the normal tail, finally returning 0 (error is cleared at the end); EMSGSIZE clears TF_TSO if used, may update the MSS from a learned MTU and retry ('goto again') if the MSS shrank, otherwise starts the pacer with 10 ms and returns the error; ENETUNREACH, EHOSTDOWN, EHOSTUNREACH and ENETDOWN record a soft error and clear the error if a SYN has been received, then like other errors start the pacer with 10 ms and return the error. After a successful send it updates rcv_adv and last_ack_sent, clears TF_ACKNOW and TF_DELACK, computes the next pacing slot with rack_get_pacing_delay when appropriate (no further send after a RST), may set up fast output for the next segment, loops ('goto again') when more can be sent in this call, and finally makes snd_nxt at least snd_max, starts the hpts timer and returns the error (0 for success). The function also returns EHOSTUNREACH if a UDP tunnelling port was removed (rack.c:21268).

name: rack_inherit
prose: rack_inherit(tp, parent) is called when a new connection tp is created from a listening parent inpcb; it returns void. If the parent's stack (t_fb) is not the same as tp's, or either connection's RACK control block pointer is NULL, it only logs (tcp_log_socket_option) and returns. Otherwise it copies from the parent's RACK state to tp's each option field that differs (including turning on dgp via rack_set_dgp, the rxt options, pacing and measurement options, the data-after-close flag and the lesser-lt-bw flags), counting the changed fields in cnt, and logs the count with tcp_log_socket_option(tp, 0, cnt, 0). The comment says the parent should be read-locked while this runs; the function itself takes no lock.

name: rack_timer_start
prose: rack_timer_start(tp, rack, cts, sup_rack) decides which RACK-stack timer to run and returns its timeout in microseconds, setting the matching PACE_TMR_* flag in rack->r_ctl.rc_hpts_flags. It returns 0 and changes nothing if rack->t_timers_stopped is set. If rack->rc_in_persist is set it returns rack_get_persists_timer_val(tp, rack) (which sets PACE_TMR_PERSIT; rc_on_min_to is not touched; it indexes tcp_backoff by t_rxtshift). Otherwise it clears rc_on_min_to. It then takes the retransmit (RXT) branch when the state is before ESTABLISHED, SACK is not permitted, the transmit-order list rc_tmap is empty or sup_rack is set; the RXT branch sets PACE_TMR_RXT only when snd_una < snd_max or the send buffer holds data, and returns tp->t_rxtcur reduced by the time since the last send or timer (or rc_min_to if it would not remain positive; at least 1), with a cap derived from the KEEPINIT timeout before establishment; if neither condition holds it returns 0 and sets no flag. Otherwise it picks the first entry of rc_tmap (the lowest un-SACKed one if that was SACKed). If that entry has SACK_PASSED, RWND_COLLAPSED or dupack >= DUP_ACK_THRESHOLD it uses the RACK timer: unless only a FIN is outstanding (then RXT) or, with PRR active in fast recovery and fewer than one segment of PRR credit, in which case it goes to the TLP branch, it computes a RACK threshold and returns the time until last send + threshold, or rc_min_to if that is not in the future or below the minimum (setting rc_on_min_to when r_rr_config == 3), and sets PACE_TMR_RACK. In the TLP branch (also reached for the PRR case) it falls back to the RXT branch when a TLP is in progress and the TLP count limit is reached, when there is no last entry in rc_tmap, when that entry holds the FIN, or when the TLP timeout would exceed TICKS_2_USEC(tcp_rexmit_max); otherwise it returns the TLP threshold minus the time since the last send (rc_min_to if that is not positive), at least rack_tlp_min and at least 1, and sets PACE_TMR_TLP. It takes no locks.
note: reviewer round15 right: PRR starvation goes to the TLP branch (activate_tlp, rack.c:6101-6114), not to RXT; round2 right: the persist path returns before rc_on_min_to is cleared (6011-6015); rack.c:5993-6218

name: rack_update_rtt
prose: rack_update_rtt(tp, rack, rsm, to, cts, ack_type, th_ack) tries to take an RTT sample from the send-map entry rsm; it returns 1 if a sample was accepted and 0 if not. It returns 0 immediately, changing nothing, if rsm is already RACK_ACKED or RACK_WAS_ACKED or r_no_rtt_allowed is set. If the entry was sent once (r_rtr_cnt == 1) it computes t from cts and the send time, updates tp->t_rttlow and rc_rack_min_rtt, passes a microsecond sample to the congestion control's rttsample callback if there is one, calls rack_apply_updated_usrtt and tcp_rack_xmit_timer (with confidence 2 for a SACKed entry, or computed from app-limited state for a cumulatively acked one), signals CC_NDUPACK for an acked TLP when not in fast recovery and rc_tlp_cwnd_reduce is set, updates rc_rack_tmit_time and rc_rack_rtt if this send is more recent, and returns 1. If the entry was retransmitted, it first sets t_rxtshift and t_softerror to 0 and recomputes t_rxtcur; then with a timestamp echo on a cumulative ack (and not RACK_OVERMAX) it finds which transmission the echo matches: for a match that is not the last transmission it returns 0 (spurious retransmission) after calling the CC callback, for a match on the last transmission it updates t_rttlow, rc_rack_min_rtt, rc_rack_tmit_time and rc_rack_rtt, calls tcp_rack_xmit_timer and returns 1; with no match, or when there is no timestamp, SACKed, or otherwise, it uses the last send time to compute t: if rc_rack_min_rtt is non-zero and t is smaller than it, it returns 0 (improper retransmit); if rc_rack_min_rtt is non-zero otherwise it only updates rc_rack_tmit_time and rc_rack_rtt when this send is newer (rc_rack_min_rtt is not changed there, because t is not below it) and returns 1; if rc_rack_min_rtt is 0 it returns 0.

name: rack_need_set_test
prose: rack_need_set_test(tp, rack, rsm, th_ack, line, use_which) restarts the goodput (gput) measurement point after an ACK; it returns void and changes state only if TF_GPUTINPROG is set in tp->t_flags and rsm->r_end >= tp->gput_seq. If rsm was transmitted more than once (r_rtr_cnt > 1) it returns without any change. Otherwise it clears rack->app_limited_needs_set, sets tp->gput_ts to the receive time, and moves tp->gput_seq: to rsm->r_start when use_which is RACK_USE_BEG and r_start >= gput_seq; to rsm->r_end when RACK_USE_END and r_end >= gput_seq; and for RACK_USE_END_OR_THACK to th_ack if th_ack is beyond rsm->r_end, else to rsm->r_end. It sets rc_gp_output_ts to the first send time of the send-map entry found at gput_seq (when gput_seq < snd_max and an entry exists); otherwise to rsm's first send time and sets app_limited_needs_set to 1. If gput_seq is beyond gput_ack it recomputes gput_ack as gput_seq plus max(initial window, MIN_GP_WIN * maxseg) when rc_gp_filled is 0, else plus the measurement window. It clears measure_saw_probe_rtt when not in probe RTT, the flag is set and gput_seq >= rc_probertt_sndmax_atexit. If rc_gp_filled is set and the window gput_ack - gput_seq is smaller than max(initial window, MIN_GP_WIN * maxseg), it either clears TF_GPUTINPROG (when the ideal measurement window exceeds the data in the send buffer) or sets gput_ack to gput_seq plus the ideal window. It then calls rack_tend_gp_marks and rack_log_gpset.
note: reviewers right: original (rc_gp_output_ts from the entry at gput_seq), round2 (RACK_USE_BEG only if r_start >= gput_seq), round15 (max(rc_init_window, MIN_GP_WIN*maxseg), not just the initial window); rack.c:9020-9172

name: tcp_respond
prose: tcp_respond(tp, ipgen, th, m, ack, seq, flags) builds and sends one TCP segment (usually an ACK or RST) in reply to a segment or from a connection template; it returns void. tp and m must not both be NULL; ipgen points to the IPv4 or IPv6 header (its version selects the family) and th to the TCP header (inside m if m is non-NULL); the network epoch is entered and, if tp is non-NULL, the inpcb lock is held. If m is NULL it allocates a new header mbuf (returning silently if allocation fails) and copies the template headers from ipgen and th without swapping addresses or ports (the template is already addressed from this side), and forces flags to TH_ACK. If m is not writable or a UDP tunnelling port is in use, it allocates a new mbuf (freeing m and returning on failure of allocation or of m_dup_pkthdr), copies the headers into it with addresses and ports swapped, and frees m. Otherwise it reuses m: the chain after the first mbuf is freed and addresses and ports are swapped in place. The window is 0 for a RST, and otherwise the receive buffer space capped at TCP_MAXWIN << rcv_scale, shifted down by rcv_scale. It adds timestamp (and, with TF_SIGNATURE, TCP-MD5) options when tp is non-NULL and TF_NOOPT is clear (a failed TCP-MD5 signature frees the mbuf and returns), sets lengths, ECN bits, hop limit or TTL, checksums, logs a server RST via tcp_log_end_status when tp is non-NULL and TH_RST is set, updates TCP statistics, and sends the packet with ip_output or ip6_output, which consume the mbuf. The mbuf passed in is always consumed.

name: tcp_default_ctloutput
prose: tcp_default_ctloutput(tp, sopt) is the default TCP-level getsockopt/setsockopt handler (tcp_usrreq.c:2020-~2640; the packet calls it tcp_ctloutput; the slice is the tail of it). It is called with the inpcb write lock held for the connection tp; sopt describes a TCP-level option and sopt_dir is SOPT_SET or SOPT_GET. It returns 0 on success or an errno: EINVAL, EPERM, ENOPROTOOPT, EFAULT, ENOENT, EOPNOTSUPP, ECONNABORTED when INP_WLOCK_RECHECK finds the inpcb dropped after the lock was released for a copyin, or an error propagated from sooptcopyin, sooptcopyout, TCPMD5_PCBCTL, the tcp_log_* helpers, stats_blob_snapshot or the KTLS helpers. The inpcb write lock is released before it returns (by the function or, on some paths, by the helper it calls). The TCP_STATS option additionally unholds the pages it held and on success sets sopt_valsize to the snapshot size.

name: in6p_join_group
prose: in6p_join_group(inp, sopt) joins an IPv6 multicast group (optionally source-specific) for the socket's inpcb; it handles IPV6_JOIN_GROUP, MCAST_JOIN_GROUP and MCAST_JOIN_SOURCE_GROUP and returns EOPNOTSUPP for any other sopt_name. The caller holds inp's write lock. Before it takes IN6_MULTI_LOCK it can return, without releasing inp: the sooptcopyin error, EADDRNOTAVAIL (unknown interface index, or the interface is missing or not IFF_MULTICAST), EINVAL (non-AF_INET6 or wrong-length group or source sockaddr, source address that is multicast, or group address that is not multicast) and EOPNOTSUPP. After taking IN6_MULTI_LOCK it finds the inpcb's membership for the group; if none exists and IPV6_MAX_MEMBERSHIPS are already joined it fails with ENOMEM; if one exists, a join with a source on an exclusive-mode membership fails with EINVAL, a join with a source already in the filter list fails with EADDRNOTAVAIL, and a join without a source fails with EADDRINUSE. Otherwise a new filter is allocated for a new membership (ENOMEM on failure), the source (if any) is grafted into the include list (ENOMEM on failure), and for a new membership it takes a reference on inp, drops the inp lock, calls in6_joingroup_locked, re-takes the lock and returns ENXIO if the inp was freed meanwhile, or the join error; for an existing membership it merges the filter state (in6m_merge) and calls mld_change_state. On success the filter state is committed (so a join with a source on an existing inclusive membership just adds a source) and it returns 0. On all paths after IN6_MULTI_LOCK it releases the inp write lock (unless the inp was freed) and IN6_MULTI_LOCK, and frees an unused new filter.

name: ip6_tryforward
prose: ip6_tryforward(m) is the IPv6 fast-forwarding path (ip6_fastfwd.c:96-331). It returns the mbuf m unchanged when the packet must go through the slow path in ip6_input (broadcast/multicast mbuf, hop-by-hop options, multicast, link-local or unspecified source or destination, or a destination that is a local address) or when a firewall hook sets M_FASTFWD_OURS (both before and after the outgoing hook); otherwise it returns NULL, after either forwarding the packet with the output interface's if_output or dropping it. The packet is dropped (and freed unless an ICMPv6 error consumed it) for: zero payload length (jumbogram), packet shorter than the IPv6 header's payload length, hop limit of 1 or less (ICMPv6 time exceeded, unless ip6stealth), pfil rejection, no route (ip6_findroute), and packets larger than the next hop's MTU (ICMPv6 packet too big); over-long packets are trimmed. A packet filter may change the destination or attach a next hop, in which case the route lookup is redone. On the forward path it decrements the hop limit (unless ip6stealth), completes delayed TCP/UDP and SCTP checksums if the interface does not do them, and calls if_output, updating the forward or discard statistics according to its result. The slice shows the tail of the function.

name: ip6_process_hopopts
prose: ip6_process_hopopts(m, opthead, hbhlen, rtalertp, plenp) walks the options of an IPv6 hop-by-hop options header (the packet name ip6_hbh_options does not exist; ip6_input.c:1019-1143). opthead points into m's data and the bytes opthead..opthead+hbhlen must be contiguous. Pad1 and PadN options are skipped (a PadN's declared length is not checked against the remaining length; a final option that overruns simply ends the loop with 0). A Router Alert option stores its 16-bit value in host order in *rtalertp. A Jumbo Payload option stores its length in *plenp. Unknown options are passed to ip6_unknown_opt according to the option's action bits (skip, silently discard, ICMP even if multicast, or ICMP if not multicast). It returns 0 on success (m not freed). It returns -1, with m freed either by m_freem or by icmp6_error, when: an option with fewer bytes remaining than its minimum header length (PadN, Router Alert, Jumbo or unknown option) is found (counted as toosmall, m_freem); a Router Alert or Jumbo option has the wrong length (ICMP parameter problem); a Jumbo option appears while the IPv6 header's payload length is non-zero; a second Jumbo option is found (*plenp already non-zero); a Jumbo length is 65535 or less; or ip6_unknown_opt requests discarding.
note: reviewer round15 right: PadN/unknown option lengths that exceed hbhlen are not rejected; the loop just ends and 0 is returned (ip6_input.c:1029-1040, 1136-1138)

name: ip6_output
prose: ip6_output(m0, opt, ro, flags, im6o, ifpp, inp) sends an IPv6 packet (ip6_output.c:403-1294; the packet shows two interior fragments). It always consumes m0 and the extension-header mbufs it builds, except that some failure returns before the packet is queued are described below. Errors and exits: EOPNOTSUPP for an unspecified source address without IPV6_UNSPECSRC or a multicast source address; EINVAL when the packet options contain a routing header (routing headers are rejected unless RTHDR_SUPPORT_IMPLEMENTED is defined, which it is not here) or when the hop-by-hop options processed for a locally sourced packet are invalid; ENOBUFS when an extension header cannot be copied or built; EHOSTUNREACH for route or scope lookup failures; ENETUNREACH for multicast on an interface that is not IFF_MULTICAST; EACCES when the output packet filter drops the packet; 0 when a packet filter consumes the packet, when multicast forwarding or loopback consumes it, when the packet is queued with netisr_queue for local delivery (returning that call's result), or when it is sent; EMSGSIZE when DONTFRAG applies and the packet is larger than the link MTU, when the path MTU is below IPV6_MMTU, for a jumbo payload that would need fragmenting, or when a fragment would be smaller than 8 bytes; and the error returned by in6_selectroute, mb_unmapped_to_ext (ENOMEM mapped to ENOBUFS), ip6_output_send or ip6_fragment. If ifpp is non-NULL it is set to the output interface after routing succeeds. A destination changed by a packet filter, or a changed FIB, causes the route lookup to be redone. An unfragmented packet is sent with ip6_output_send. If fragmentation fails, the fragments already made are freed (not sent) and the non-zero ip6_fragment error is returned; otherwise each fragment is sent with ip6_output_send, and after the first send error the remaining fragments are freed and that error is returned; ip6s_fragmented is counted only when every fragment was sent.
note: slice cut the head; reviewer round15 right: a fragmentation or fragment-send error frees the fragments and returns non-zero (ip6_output.c:1248-1279); the mb_unmapped_to_ext failure return at line 1114 relies on that helper freeing the chain, not verified here

name: ip6_ctloutput
prose: ip6_ctloutput(so, sopt) handles getsockopt and setsockopt at the IPPROTO_IPV6 level and a few SOL_SOCKET options for IPv6 sockets (ip6_output.c:1576-~2400). The inpcb is obtained with sotoinpcb(so) and the caller holds no inpcb lock; locks are taken inside as needed. It returns 0 on success, or an errno such as EINVAL, ENOPROTOOPT, EOPNOTSUPP, EPERM, ENOBUFS, EISCONN, EFAULT or one propagated from sooptcopyin, soopt_mcopyin, sooptcopyout, sosetfib, ip6_pcbopts, ip6_pcbopt, ip6_setmoptions or IPSEC_PCBCTL. An unhandled option name at the IPPROTO_IPV6 level returns ENOPROTOOPT, and an invalid sopt_dir returns EINVAL. Setting the options IPV6_HOPLIMIT, IPV6_TCLASS, IPV6_DONTFRAG, IPV6_USE_MIN_MTU, IPV6_PREFER_TEMPADDR and the advanced-API packet options returns ECONNRESET, with the inpcb write lock released, when the inpcb has been dropped. For IPV6_2292PKTOPTIONS/IPV6_PKTOPTIONS set, the option mbuf m obtained with soopt_getm is freed after ip6_pcbopts, but if soopt_getm or soopt_mcopyin fails the function breaks out with the error and m is not freed by this code. For SOPT_GET most values are copied out with sooptcopyout, and IPV6_2292PKTOPTIONS/IPV6_PKTOPTIONS get a size of 0.

name: mld_v2_enqueue_group_record
prose: mld_v2_enqueue_group_record(mq, inm, is_state_change, is_group_query, is_source_query, use_block_allow) appends an MLDv2 group record for membership inm to the report queue mq; the caller holds the IN6 multicast list lock. It returns the number of bytes appended (nbytes), 0 when nothing needed to be appended (no change to report, or a source query that finds no recorded sources), or a negative errno (-ENOMEM) when the queue is full or an mbuf allocation or m_append fails; when only the filter list changed it returns the result of mld_v2_enqueue_filter_change instead. The record type is chosen from the old and new filter modes (a current-state record when is_state_change is 0). It appends to the tail packet of mq if is_group_query is 0, the packet has room and fewer than MLD_V2_REPORT_MAXRECS records, otherwise it allocates a new packet; then it appends the group record and as many in-mode sources (recorded ones only when is_source_query) as fit; further packets are allocated for remaining sources. On -ENOMEM, a packet that was allocated by the failing step is freed if it is not the reused tail packet, but packets already enqueued in earlier steps stay in the queue. The returned byte count adds the sources of the first packet twice (once per source and again after the loop), so it overstates the data by msrcs * sizeof(struct in6_addr) for that first packet.

name: nd6_na_input
prose: nd6_na_input(m, off, icmp6len) processes an ICMPv6 neighbor advertisement; it returns void and consumes m on every path. The caller is in the network epoch (assert); m_pkthdr.rcvif is the receiving interface. The mbuf is freed without further action for fragmented packets, invalid ND options, NAs for a CARP address when we are not the CARP master, NAs for our own addresses (a tentative address calls nd6_dad_na_input, any other own address is logged), a missing neighbor entry, and static entries. A hop limit other than 255, a multicast target, a solicited advertisement sent to a multicast destination, a failed in6_setscope or a target link-layer address option of the wrong length is counted as a bad NA (icp6s_badna) and freed; a failed m_pullup frees the chain and returns. For an entry that is INCOMPLETE it records the link-layer address (an NA without a link-layer option is ignored on links that have addresses), sets the state to REACHABLE if solicited, STALE otherwise, remembers the router flag and, if the router flag is set, calls pfxlist_onlink_check() at the end. For other entries it applies the override/solicited/lladdr rules of RFC 4861 (changing the address, state and, when the router flag was dropped, removing the default router or flushing routes); pfxlist_onlink_check is not called in that case. It resets la_asked, grabs the hold chain, and at the end unlocks the entry, flushes the hold chain (and the children's chain after resolving an INCOMPLETE entry) and frees m.

name: defrouter_select_fib
prose: defrouter_select_fib(fibnum) chooses and installs the default router for one FIB; it returns void. If fibnum is RT_ALL_FIBS it calls itself for every FIB from 0 to rt_numfibs - 1 and returns. Otherwise, holding the ND6 read lock and the network epoch, it does nothing if the default router list is empty. It scans the list considering only routers whose ifp->if_fib equals fibnum: the first reachable one (is_dr_reachable) becomes selected_dr and the router marked installed becomes installed_dr (a second installed router is logged as an error); each is referenced. If no router was found reachable, it scans forward through the list (TAILQ_FOREACH_FROM, no wraparound) starting at the head when no router is installed or the installed one is the last list entry, otherwise at the entry after the installed router, and selects the first router found for this FIB (none if there is no such router). If a reachable router was selected and an installed router exists, the installed router is kept when it is still reachable and rtpref(selected) <= rtpref(installed). After dropping the ND6 lock, if the selected and installed routers differ it deletes the installed router's route (defrouter_delreq) if there is one and adds the selected router's route (defrouter_addreq) if there is one. It then releases the temporary references it took. No routing change is made when no router for fibnum is found.

name: rip6_input
prose: rip6_input(mp, offp, proto) delivers a received IPv6 packet to the raw sockets that match it; it always returns IPPROTO_DONE and always consumes the mbuf *mp (the pointer is not changed). The caller is in the network epoch. It iterates over the raw IPv6 PCBs matching protocol and addresses (each locked for reading). For each PCB it skips the socket if the IPsec policy check fails, if a jailed socket without its own vnet is not permitted the destination address, if it is bound to another FIB (unless V_rip_bind_all_fibs), or if it has multicast options that filter out a multicast destination (MLD traffic with M_RTALERT_MLD is exempt), and skips it if m_copym fails. If the PCB has a checksum offset set and the checksum is bad, the PCB lock is released, proto is set to IPPROTO_NONE and the whole loop stops (so remaining PCBs get no copy, while copies already delivered stay). Otherwise it copies the packet, saves control information if the socket wants it, strips the headers and appends the data with the source address to the socket's receive buffer; if sbappendaddr fails it calls soroverflow, frees the copy and counts rip6s_fullsock, else it wakes the reader and counts the delivery. If no socket received a copy, it counts rip6s_nosock and frees m: with proto == IPPROTO_NONE it is freed silently, otherwise icmp6_error sends a parameter problem (unrecognised next header) and consumes it; ip6s_delivered is decremented. If at least one socket received a copy, m is freed.

name: sctp6_getaddr
prose: sctp6_getaddr(so, sa) fills the sockaddr_in6 at sa with the socket's local address and returns 0 or an errno. It first zeroes the whole structure and sets sin6_len and sin6_family = AF_INET6 (so on every error return the port and address fields are zero, except where noted). It returns ECONNRESET if the socket has no SCTP inpcb. With the inpcb read-locked it sets sin6_port to the local port. For a bound-all socket that is connected, it takes the first association, finds the first of its nets with an IPv6 address and sets sin6_addr from sctp_source_address_selection (left zero if that returns no address); with no association or no IPv6 net it returns ENOENT (sin6_port already set). For a bound-all socket that is not connected, sin6_addr is the unspecified address. For a socket not bound to all, sin6_addr is the first IPv6 address in the local address list, or ENOENT if there is none (port already set). After releasing the lock it calls sa6_recoverscope and returns its error if non-zero (the port and address have then been written); otherwise it returns 0.
note: reviewers right: original (sa6_recoverscope error return; port already set on ENOENT) and round15 (the initial compound literal zeroes all fields, sctp6_usrreq.c:897-900); sctp6_usrreq.c:889-979

name: sctp6_peeraddr
prose: sctp6_peeraddr(so, sa) fills the sockaddr_in6 at sa with the peer's address and returns 0 or an errno. It first zeroes the whole structure and sets sin6_len and sin6_family = AF_INET6. It returns ENOTCONN if the socket has no SCTP inpcb or the inpcb is not connected, and ECONNRESET if the connected inpcb has no association. Otherwise it takes the first association (holding its TCB lock), finds the first net with an IPv6 address and copies that address and the association's remote port into sa, then releases the TCB lock. If no net has an IPv6 address it returns ENOENT (port and address stay zero). It then calls sa6_recoverscope and returns its error if non-zero (the port and address have already been written), else 0.
note: reviewers right: original (sa6_recoverscope error) and round15 (all fields are zeroed first, sctp6_usrreq.c:992-995); sctp6_usrreq.c:982-1036

name: udp6_send
prose: udp6_send(so, flags_arg, m, addr6, control, td) sends a UDP or UDP-Lite datagram on an IPv6 socket (the packet's name udp6_sendto does not exist; udp6_usrreq.c:676-981). The function takes the inpcb lock itself (write lock when addr6 is NULL, or when the socket has no local address and no local port, otherwise a read lock) and enters the network epoch for the output part; the caller must not hold the inpcb lock. It always consumes m and control. Errors: EAFNOSUPPORT if addr6 is not AF_INET6, EINVAL for a wrong sa_len or an IPv6-only socket given a v4-mapped destination, the error from sa6_embedscope, the error from ip6_setpktopts, EADDRNOTAVAIL for destination port 0, EISCONN if a destination is given on a connected socket, the error from in6_selectsrc_socket, the error from in6_pcbsetport (with the inpcb local address reset to in6addr_any), ENOTCONN if addr6 is NULL on an unconnected socket, ENOBUFS if the header cannot be prepended, and the error from ip6_output. On a non-IPv6-only socket, if the destination (or the connected address) is v4-mapped, the lock is released and the datagram is handed to udp_send with PRUS_IPV6 added to the flags, returning its result. On success it builds the UDP header (UDP-Lite coverage handling), the IPv6 header and checksum and calls ip6_output, returning its result. On every path the inpcb lock is released and the epoch exited before returning, any control mbuf has its packet options cleared and is freed, and m is freed on failure paths (consumed by ip6_output on the send path).

name: frrequest
prose: frrequest(softc, unit, req, data, set, makecopy) handles ioctl requests that add, insert, remove or zero IPFilter rules (fil.c:4439-~5100; the packet's name for the slice is an unnamed fragment of this function). If makecopy is non-zero, data is a user rule: it is copied in with ipf_inobj, and the function returns the copyin error, EINVAL if the rule is a built-in type, shorter than frentry_t, has a size not equal to sizeof(frentry_t) plus the name length, or a name length outside 0..ipf_max_namelen, and ENOMEM if the rule buffer cannot be allocated; the copied rule has its list pointers cleared and FR_COPIED set, and each name string in it is validated (EINVAL on failure, via donenolock which frees the copy). If makecopy is zero, data is a kernel (built-in) rule and EINVAL is returned if it is not marked built-in. Further checks (data size and pointer consistency, and so on) give EINVAL. For a zero-statistics request (OP_ZERO) the matching rule's counters are copied out to the caller and zeroed only if the copy out succeeded, ESRCH if no rule matches, EFAULT on a failed copyout, the temporary copy freed and the ipf_mutex released before returning. Add and insert requests place the rule in the list or group chosen by its fr_collect field. The slice shown is a middle fragment; the ipf_mutex write lock taken in the function is released on its return paths.

name: ipf_token_find
prose: ipf_token_find(softc, type, uid, ptr) looks up or creates a token for the tuple (ptr, type, uid) in softc's ipf_token list and returns it with a reference held for the caller, or NULL. It first allocates and zeroes a new token (KMALLOC) in case it is needed, then takes the ipf_tokens write lock and searches the list for a token with the same context pointer, type and uid and with ipt_complete < 2. If none is found it uses the new token (setting ipt_ctx, ipt_uid, ipt_type and ipt_ref = 1), or returns NULL (releasing the lock) if the allocation had failed. If one is found the spare allocation is freed; if the found token has ipt_complete > 0 (that is 1) the result is NULL; otherwise the token is unlinked from its position. A token to be returned is appended at the tail of the list, its ipt_ref is incremented (so a new token ends with 2) and ipt_die is set to ipf_ticks + 20. The lock is released before returning.

name: ipf_frag_deref
prose: ipf_frag_deref(arg, frp[, lock]) is a static function (the lock parameter exists only with USE_MUTEXES) that drops one reference on a fragment-cache entry. It reads the entry from *frp and sets *frp to NULL unconditionally (so the caller can no longer use the pointer, even when the entry is not freed), takes the lock for writing, decrements the entry's ipfr_ref, and calls ipf_frag_free(softf, entry) if the count is now zero or less; then it releases the lock. It returns void.

name: ipf_log_items
prose: ipf_log_items(softc, unit, fin, items, itemsz, types, cnt) appends one log record built from cnt items (copied with bcopy for type 0 and with COPYDATA from an mbuf for type 1, after an iplog_t header with magic, sequence number, size and kernel time) to the log queue of the device unit. It returns 0 on success and -1 when the record is not logged. It raises the spl level, takes ipl_mutex[unit] and increments ipl_counter[unit] (on every path). If the used log space plus the record length would exceed the log size, or the buffer cannot be allocated, it increments ipl_logfail[unit], releases the mutex and returns -1 (this path does not restore the saved spl level). Otherwise it copies the items; if suppression is enabled (ipl_suppress) and fin is non-NULL with fin_off == 0 and the previous record (ipll[unit]) exists with the same CRC and the first FI_LCSIZE bytes of fin equal, it increments that previous record's count, releases the mutex, restores the spl level, frees the new buffer and returns 0. In all other cases it saves fin's data for the next comparison (or clears it when suppression is on and fin does not qualify), counts ipl_logok, links the new record at the tail, adds its length to ipl_used[unit], releases the mutex, wakes readers (WAKEUP and POLLWAKEUP, or cv_signal and pollwakeup on Solaris), restores the spl level and returns 0; the queue then owns the buffer.

name: ipf_nat_ioctl
prose: ipf_nat_ioctl(softc, data, cmd, mode, uid, ctx) is IPFilter's NAT ioctl handler (ip_nat.c:973-~1500; the slice shows its first part). On FreeBSD it returns EPERM if FWRITE is set in mode and securelevel is 3 or higher, and EOPNOTSUPP for a jailed caller without a vnet. getlock is false when NAT_LOCKHELD is set in mode. For SIOCADNAT, SIOCRMNAT and SIOCPURGENAT the rule (an ipnat_t) is read from data (copied with ipf_inobj/ipf_inobjsz unless NAT_SYSSPACE is set): EFAULT-type errors from the copy routines are returned, EINVAL for in_size smaller than ipnat_t, in_size different from sizeof(ipnat_t) plus in_namelen, in_namelen out of range or invalid name strings, ENOMEM if the rule buffer cannot be allocated, and the error from ipf_nat_rule_init; the rule is then looked up in the NAT rule list under ipf_nat_io. SIOCADNAT needs FWRITE (EPERM otherwise), returns EEXIST (copying the found rule out first) if an identical rule exists, ENOMEM if there is no copied rule, and otherwise calls ipf_nat_siocaddnat to link it in (ownership of the allocated rule passes to the list on success). SIOCRMNAT and SIOCPURGENAT need FWRITE (EPERM) and an existing rule (ESRCH); SIOCPURGENAT first copies the rule out to data with ipf_outobjsz and only afterwards sets IPN_PURGE on the list entry, so the copied-out rule does not carry IPN_PURGE; then ipf_nat_siocdelnat removes the rule. The other commands handled in the switch include the NAT log commands (SIOCIPFFB, SIOCSETLG, SIOCGETLG, FIONREAD), SIOCGNATS (statistics) and further lookup, iterator and table commands not shown in the slice, each returning 0, EPERM, EFAULT or the delegated helper's error as appropriate; an unknown command returns EINVAL. The ipf_nat_io mutex is released on all paths on which it was taken and temporary rule copies are freed on failure.
